name: Face Alignment
mechanism:
This method analyzes facial alignment and landmark stability for video deepfake detection:

1. **Dense Facial Landmark Tracking**: A dense set of facial landmarks (68-468 points) is tracked per frame. Landmark positions are analyzed for both absolute accuracy (correct facial geometry) and temporal stability (smooth motion trajectories).

2. **Geometric Consistency Verification**: Facial landmark geometry must conform to anthropometric constraints — inter-ocular distance vs. face width ratios, nose-mouth proportions, and facial thirds (forehead, nose, chin). The method checks whether geometric ratios remain consistent across frames and fall within normal human ranges. Deepfakes may produce faces with fluctuating proportions.

3. **Landmark Jitter Analysis**: In authentic video, facial landmarks follow smooth trajectories governed by musculoskeletal dynamics. The method measures high-frequency landmark position variations (jitter). Elevated jitter — particularly at face boundary landmarks — indicates deepfake artifacts from frame-independent face generation or imperfect face-to-background alignment.

4. **Pose-Corrected Alignment**: Landmarks are corrected for 3D head pose (yaw, pitch, roll) to evaluate face structure independent of viewing angle. After pose correction, facial proportions should remain constant. Deepfakes may produce pose-dependent proportion changes, indicating the generator doesn't maintain consistent 3D face geometry.

5. **Alignment Boundary Analysis**: The alignment between generated face landmarks and background facial context (hairline, ears, neck) is checked. Misalignment at the face-swap boundary — where generated landmarks don't smoothly transition to background anatomy — indicates deepfake manipulation.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through face alignment analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video

references.title: Rossler, A. et al. (2019). FaceForensics++: Learning to Detect Manipulated Facial Images. ICCV.
Yang, X. et al. (2019). Exposing Deep Fakes Using Inconsistent Head Poses. ICASSP.
